tasks.short: Participate in campus and community events

steps.what: Participate in campus and community events and engage with attendees

tasks.design: Retain personal participation and attendee dialogue. Event details may remain in {CALENDAR}; this task does not establish an event-administration or report-writing baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Community engagement requires presence, listening and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling software does not perform the participation itself.
tasks.still_hard: Responding meaningfully to different interests and representing professional knowledge appropriately.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices the question behind an attendee's concern and builds trust through a direct response.
tasks.altitude: Event participation time and representative responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss a shared community health-education concern with attendees

evidence.claim: Personal event participation is relationship work; calendar capabilities alone do not establish a labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is teacher participation, excluding organiser labour and event administration.
Participants produce and clarify questions in retained s1; no structured attendee-needs record is assumed.
Existing calendar access is baseline; check native functions before future custom work. No public statements or commitments are automated.
No new software or maintained process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Are any measured participation barriers due to administrative work outside this boundary?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and demanding events retain participation time; no organiser paperwork is transferred into the teacher baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select lecture objectives, current sources and appropriate health-specialty examples
Prepare lecture outline, examples and explanatory materials from checked sources

loop.input: Teacher brief and selected source passages
loop.output: Draft outline and explanations with source links
loop.check: Teacher compares claims, clinical qualifiers and examples to sources and learning objectives
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported explanations require manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting explanations to prior knowledge needs language judgement beyond layout templates

steps.what: Check lecture accuracy, sequence and accessibility before teaching
Deliver lectures and respond to undergraduate or graduate students' questions

tasks.design: Use native templates in {DOCS} and presentation software {OTHER}, with a bounded drafting loop only for explanations based on selected sources. The teacher checks the complete lecture, then retains delivery and student interaction; no clinical advice or student grading is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning selected evidence into clear explanations repeats some prose work.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-restricted drafting can shorten rewriting while templates handle fixed structure.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what matters, preserving clinical qualifications and responding to misunderstanding during teaching.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices when an explanation fails and develops a better one with the class.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation rewriting; source appraisal, final checking and live teaching keep their time.

reach.task: Check a lecture example against the stated learning objective

evidence.claim: Restricted-source lecture drafting may reduce rewriting with teacher checks and live teaching retained; the estimate is model knowledge, not a case from the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is lecture preparation and delivery, excluding examinations, student assessment and private clinical records.
Teacher produces topic, audience level, objectives, source title, version, passages and permitted examples in s1 with all 15 hours retained. No ready verified lecture brief is assumed.
s2 retains 12 hours for prompt capture, claim checks and editing; s3 retains all final checking. Unsupported sources return to manual writing; no invented references are accepted.
Test native templates and reuse of approved materials before a loop. Existing presentation features earn no new gain. Only authorised public or teacher-owned material enters the drafting environment.
unknowns: Current preparation burden and available approved sources
Institutional drafting policy and presentation tools
research_questions: Does source-restricted drafting reduce total preparation while preserving clinical qualifications and student understanding?

incremental.description: Maintain templates, refresh sources and audit draft changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=15+12+10+55=92; gross 8 minus 3 upkeep gives net 5. High requires repeated explanatory drafting; low removes only 3 hours, offset by upkeep. Source selection, final checks and delivery retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform departmental administration and leadership duties

steps.what: Review department needs and decide administrative priorities with relevant colleagues
Perform administrative duties by recording agreed departmental actions and assignments
Coordinate department activities and resolve staff or administrative exceptions

tasks.design: Configure native action forms in {PROJECT} linked to controlled department records in {DOCS}. The teacher records agreed decisions with reusable identifiers while retaining leadership judgement, staff discussion and exception resolution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed actions can be re-entered across administrative records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms and linked records can reduce duplicate entry.
tasks.still_hard: Prioritising resources and resolving conflicting staff and institutional needs.
tasks.human_edge: The department leader can recognise when a technically complete action would be unfair or impractical.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated action entry; leadership and employment authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Trace a recorded action to its agreed owner and deadline

evidence.claim: Native action forms can reduce duplicate administrative entry while departmental decisions remain human; the allocation is modelled.

assumptions: Boundary is routine department leadership administration, excluding specialised HR, budget approval or formal academic decisions.
Teacher produces action, rationale, owner and deadline in retained s1. s2 retains 22.5 hours for capture, identifiers, record checks and manual exceptions; no ready coded decision is assumed.
Missing or disputed actions return to manual clarification. No automatic staffing, budget or academic action is taken and no staff evaluation dashboard is introduced.
Test native forms first; existing linked records earn no new gain. National staff-consultation and access requirements are checked in rollout.
unknowns: Department duty mix and actual duplicated entry
Native action tools and decision authority
research_questions: Can linked action records reduce repeated entry without losing decision context or changing who may decide?

incremental.description: Maintain forms, access and action mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=40+22.5+30=92.5; gross 7.5 minus 2 upkeep gives net 5.5. High assumes repeated action entry; low removes only 2 hours, offset by upkeep. Leadership and coordination keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write proposals for external research funding

steps.what: Define research design, funding fit and verified grant proposal inputs
Write grant proposal sections from the research design and checked evidence

loop.purpose: Draft funder-specific narrative from researcher-owned verified inputs
loop.input: Verified brief, budget assumptions, references and call requirements
loop.output: Source-linked proposal draft with unsupported sections flagged
loop.check: Teacher checks novelty claims, methods, commitments, budget narrative and each citation against the actual inputs
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or conflicting requirements return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Connecting a novel research argument to call criteria needs language judgement beyond form assembly

steps.what: Check the complete grant proposal and send it for institutional authorisation

tasks.design: Use native call templates in {DOCS}, with a bounded drafting loop only for narrative based on a verified research brief and checked budget inputs from {SPREADSHEET}. The teacher checks methods, commitments and references before sending the complete package through institutional authorisation; funder submission remains outside this writing boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adapting a developed research argument to a funder's narrative structure repeats drafting work.
tasks.enabler_now: Restricted-input drafting can shorten rewriting without inventing the research design or evidence.
tasks.still_hard: A credible novel question, feasible methods, defensible costs and genuine team commitments.
tasks.human_edge: The researcher knows what the team can actually deliver and can reject an attractive but unsupported claim.
tasks.altitude: Less narrative rewriting with research design and institutional approval unchanged.

reach.task: Check a proposal package against call conditions and institutional approval needs

evidence.claim: Restricted-input drafting can reduce funder-specific narrative rewriting while research design and final verification remain; the allocation is model knowledge.
The digest reports that NWO referees may not use generative AI and proposal uploads breach referee confidentiality; this is a referee restriction and does not establish applicant permission.

assumptions: Boundary is applicant proposal writing and internal submission, excluding peer review, final institutional approval and external funder submission.

Teacher produces question, methods, milestones, risks, team commitments, call version, reference identifiers and cost assumptions in s1, with all 40 hours retained. No ready research design or approved budget is assumed.

s2 retains 22 hours for input capture, citation resolution, claim checking and editing; s3 retains 20 hours for complete-package checks. Missing references, permissions or commitments return to manual drafting and clarification.

Test native templates and reusable approved sections before a loop. Only researcher-owned or authorised inputs enter an approved environment after institution and funder rules are checked; restricted proposals and participant data are excluded.

Existing institutional authorisation remains required before external submission. No model-produced budget approval or signature is assumed and proposal-writing gains are not claimed for referee work.
unknowns: Funder and institution applicant drafting rules
Current narrative burden and secure tool access
research_questions: Does total brief, draft and final-check time fall without unsupported novelty claims, references or commitments?

already_counted.description: Research design and structured brief capture

incremental.description: Maintain call templates, access rules and drafting quality samples

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=40+22+20=82; gross 18 minus 4 upkeep gives net 14. High requires repeated adaptation of developed research narratives; low removes only 4 hours for difficult or infrequent calls, offset by upkeep. Design and final checking retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce bounded drafting and duplicate action entry while preserving teaching, research design, leadership and community engagement.
reach: Work with research support officers on traceable proposal commitments and administrators on accurate departmental actions
role.ambitious_version: A teacher and researcher who prepares clear, checked material with less rewriting while remaining responsible for the evidence, commitments and people involved.
